title: The Fire That Fell on Elijah’s Sacrifice
paragraphs: The Fire That Fell on Elijah’s Sacrifice
You can rebuild the altar.
You can pour the water.
You can stand alone while everyone laughs.
But only God can send the fire.
On Mount Carmel, Elijah stood before a nation that had learned how to mix worship with rebellion. They still knew God’s name, but their hearts had bowed to Baal.
And God saw it.
Elijah cried, “How long will you go limping between two different opinions? If the LORD is God, follow Him.” — 1 Kings 18:21
You knew.
That is the question for every lukewarm heart.
Not, “Do you believe in God?”
But, “Why are you still divided?”
The prophets of Baal screamed. Cut themselves. Performed. Strained. Nothing answered.
Because false gods always demand blood but never give life.
Then Elijah repaired the altar of the Lord.
Read that again.
Before the fire fell, the altar was repaired.
Some of you want God’s power without surrender. You want breakthrough without repentance. You want heaven to answer while your heart still protects the idol.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
The fire did not fall on Elijah.
It fell on the sacrifice.
That points us to Jesus Christ.
At the cross, the judgment we deserved fell on the perfect Lamb of God. Our sin was exposed. Our guilt was real. But grace was greater.
“He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree.” — 1 Peter 2:24
The fire of God’s holiness fell on Christ so mercy could fall on you.
When the people saw the fire consume the sacrifice, they fell on their faces and cried, “The LORD, He is God!” — 1 Kings 18:39
That is the only right response.
Repent.
Stop limping.
Stop pretending.
Come to Jesus by faith.
Salvation is not earned by your performance. It is received by grace through faith in Christ alone.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
